title: Google Cloud Associate Cloud Engineer (ACE) Infrastructure & Kubernetes Deployment Lab
problem: Engineers preparing for the Google Cloud Associate Cloud Engineer (ACE) certification often practice solely in the graphical Cloud Console, failing to acquire the necessary proficiency in declarative Terraform infrastructure-as-code and the `gcloud` command-line interface. Consequently, when deploying containerized applications to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) or Cloud Run, they struggle with configuring least-privilege IAM service accounts, managing multi-project resource hierarchies, or automating Cloud Monitoring alert policies. This guide delivers a hands-on cloud engineering lab curriculum and reproducible deployment project in Google Cloud / local container environments. The engineer provisions Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters with autoscaling, deploys stateless microservices to Cloud Run, configures least-privilege IAM service account bindings, manages Cloud Storage bucket lifecycles, and automates Cloud Monitoring uptime alerts.

use_cases.title: Scalable Containerized Microservice Hosting on Google Kubernetes Engine
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise organizations running high-throughput APIs on Google Cloud need managed Kubernetes clusters that scale compute capacity automatically with load.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engineer provisions a GKE cluster with cluster autoscaling and node auto-provisioning, deploying containerized applications with ingress load balancing.

use_cases.title: Serverless Container Workload Deployment on Cloud Run
use_cases.first_sentence: Fast-growing digital platforms processing event webhooks require serverless execution that scales to zero during idle periods to eliminate unnecessary compute costs.
use_cases.second_sentence: The project packages microservice containers into Google Artifact Registry and deploys them to Cloud Run with automatic concurrency scaling and sub-2s cold starts.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Cloud IAM Governance & Least-Privilege Access Control
use_cases.first_sentence: Multi-team organizations sharing Google Cloud projects must isolate developer permissions and prevent cross-environment resource tampering.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system configures IAM custom roles, binds service accounts to specific resources with predefined permissions, and logs audit access events in Cloud Logging.

hard_parts: Mastering the `gcloud` CLI syntax across resource hierarchies (Organizations, Folders, Projects) for rapid declarative and imperative execution
Configuring Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster autoscaler parameters and horizontal pod autoscalers (HPA) for efficient resource bin-packing
Binding least-privilege IAM roles to compute service accounts while avoiding overly permissive primitive roles (Viewer, Editor, Owner)
Designing Cloud Storage lifecycle management rules and Cloud Monitoring alert policies with automated notification delivery
screener_signals: Clean infrastructure repository containing Terraform HCL modules, `gcloud` deployment scripts, GKE manifests, and Cloud Monitoring alert rules
Autoscaling benchmark report proving GKE cluster scales compute nodes from 2 to 5 nodes under simulated traffic load in under 180 seconds
Anti-fake verification script attempting to access a restricted Cloud Storage bucket using an unauthorized service account and asserting HTTP 403 Forbidden

architecture.data_flow: An operator authenticates via `gcloud auth`; Terraform provisions Google Cloud project resources and service accounts; container images are built via Docker and published to Artifact Registry; GKE pulls images to deploy microservices behind a Cloud Load Balancer; Cloud Run receives asynchronous webhooks with auto-scaling; static data uploads to Cloud Storage with automated lifecycle policies; Cloud Monitoring scrapes metrics across GKE, Cloud Run, and storage buckets; when an uptime check fails, Cloud Monitoring generates an incident alert; IAM policies enforce that service accounts only possess least-privilege permissions.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Google Cloud IAM policy evaluation and OAuth 2.0 bearer token validation returning HTTP 403 on permission violations.

targets.metric: Cloud Run Serverless Cold Start & Request Latency
targets.method: Wall-clock round-trip duration for a scaled-to-zero Cloud Run container to initialize and return HTTP 200 response
targets.input: 20 sequential cold-start requests issued after container scale-to-zero idle period
targets.environment: Google Cloud Run service environment running lightweight Python container
targets.minimum_pass: p95 container cold start latency is < 2.5 seconds with p95 warm latency < 45ms
targets.target: p95 container cold start latency is < 1.4 seconds with p95 warm latency < 22ms
targets.report: Cloud Run latency benchmark report and cold start distribution log

targets.metric: GKE Cluster Node Autoscaling Expansion Duration
targets.method: Elapsed time for GKE cluster autoscaler to detect pending unschedulable pods and add 3 compute nodes to node pool
targets.input: High-concurrency batch workload creating 30 compute-heavy pods exceeding baseline cluster capacity
targets.environment: GKE cluster configured with cluster autoscaler (min 2, max 5 nodes)
targets.minimum_pass: Cluster scales from 2 to 5 nodes and schedules 30 of 30 pods in < 210 seconds
targets.target: Cluster scales from 2 to 5 nodes and schedules 30 of 30 pods in < 140 seconds
targets.report: GKE autoscaling event log and node provisioning timing trace

targets.metric: Cloud Storage IAM Least-Privilege Access Enforcement Rate
targets.method: Percentage of unauthorized bucket read/write operations rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden across restricted service accounts
targets.input: 50 simulated storage API operations executed using unauthorized service account credentials
targets.environment: Google Cloud Storage bucket configured with uniform bucket-level access and restricted IAM bindings
targets.minimum_pass: 50 of 50 unauthorized storage operations rejected with HTTP 403
targets.target: 50 of 50 unauthorized storage operations rejected with HTTP 403
targets.report: Cloud Storage IAM security audit log and permission denial trace
